sonnet.problem: The question asks who brought the onyx stones and gemstones, with the choices leaders, judges or scribes. Nothing in the earlier cards makes 'leaders' a reasoned pick over the other two, so the baker can only guess. The verse is also first told inside the question itself, with no story card to set it up.
sonnet.rule: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

sonnet.problem: This card asks again about people with stirred or prompted hearts bringing an offering. That is the same point as card 6 (a willing heart), card 11 (hearts stirred bring an offering) and the card 12 story ('all with willing hearts'). Verse 29 only sums up verses 21-28, so the card tests nothing new.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question.
